scenes.title: A little help returning
utterances: Meet Mira, the face of FocusPilot: a quiet local productivity companion that helps you return to the task you meant to do.
You choose your goal and limits. Mira offers a gentle next step, while breaks, overrides and the final decision stay with you.
This is our pre-event application concept and working research, with useful pieces already tested and important physical demonstrations still ahead.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn the intended benefit → original Mira, task note and phone-shaped feed ribbon → one detour gently rejoins the task → start close on the note, pull back to the companion → note at 10%, detour at 35%, return at 65% → final task remains visible; no measured productivity claim.

scenes.title: The useful everyday loop
utterances: Imagine choosing a study task, starting focus, and setting a budget for one app that often becomes a detour during work.
An optional monitor would notice that chosen limit, explain a nudge, and offer a return. Accountability uses virtual points; no real money moves.
The product starts from your intention, not a claim that every social app or every moment of rest is unproductive.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn the proposed workflow → task note, focus clock, selected-app budget arc, virtual points → user starts a clock, an illustrative overrun offers one nudge, override returns control → wide workbench composition → goal at 10%, overrun at 40%, override at 70% → label **Intended workflow · permission testing pending**, virtual balance unchanged by override.

scenes.title: Understanding with a boundary
utterances: A small open-source Qwen model understands a request locally, then proposes a bounded action such as starting focus or opening an approved tool.
A separate validator checks the whole original request and its arguments before you review and confirm. The model cannot authorize itself to act.
In a historical phone test, alarm cancellation was wrongly proposed as creation. The independent gate rejected it, and no Clock action ran.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn why proposal differs from action → request capsule, Qwen block, validator gate and confirmation lever → supported request advances only after lever; “cancel my alarm” becomes wrong alarm proposal and visibly stops → horizontal causal path, then close on closed gate → trace before payload at 20%, failure at 55%, rejection hold at 75% → no Clock/action icon fires.

scenes.title: What the phone evidence proves
utterances: Historical version zero point six ran typed Qwen requests on the Nothing development phone. Reviewed Start and Pause actually changed focus state.
Those observations took seventeen point three two three seconds and one point eight one four seconds. They were not speech or current-version benchmarks.
Current version zero point ten has a source-bound installed package and one hundred thirty-three passing Android tests. The phone remained asleep; current actions are untested.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn evidence scope → dated v0.6 CPU timeline and separate v0.10 package envelope → confirmed historical Start changes own checkpoint active, Pause changes it paused; current package enters installed box without action arrow → split composition, never fake app UI → historical figures at 25%, date boundary at 50%, current idle state at 70% → labels **Historical typed phone test** and **Current install identity only**.

scenes.title: More useful commands, measured honestly
utterances: Fresh frozen synthetic confirmation improved correct supported proposals from fifteen to thirty-one out of fifty, with sixteen gains and no losses on that set.
Nineteen supported requests still abstained. Both gates rejected all fifty unsupported requests, with no wrong accepts observed; that is not universal safety.
Raw Qwen intent correctness was thirty-six out of one hundred, including forty-nine unsupported tool proposals. The informed author's synthetic test is not human voice evidence.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn gain and remaining coverage → fifty supported dots shared between old/new gate lanes → fifteen light, then thirty-one; nineteen stay outlined → close paired lanes with distinct abstention area, not total-accuracy headline → baseline at 15%, gains at 40%, omissions at 65% → labels **Fresh synthetic confirmation**, **16 gains · 0 losses**, **19 abstentions**; hold for reading.

scenes.title: Keep the simpler successful choice
utterances: We selected the expanded request gate for research packaging, while keeping Qwen three point five, zero point eight billion, its quantized weights and native runtime unchanged.
A longer prompt experiment was rejected because useful command understanding fell and host latency rose. More instructions were not automatically better.
Today's local backend is CPU. These host comparisons neither promise phone response times nor demonstrate Snapdragon NPU execution or autonomous reliability.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn component selection → unchanged model/prompt objects, longer prompt branch and expanded request gate → longer branch grows latency ribbon then dims; original path keeps its identity while gate gains supported wrapper tokens → cutaway of language path → candidate at 20%, rejection at 45%, retained route at 70% → **Original prompt retained · gate expanded · explicit review**.

scenes.title: Explain the small decisions
utterances: A separate sixty-five parameter network was actually trained on invented sandbox labels, reaching ninety-eight point three three percent accuracy on its synthetic holdout.
Its connections are nonnegative, its biases signed. We can inspect exact contributions and interventions, but this is not real human productivity accuracy.
The network remains a shadow explanation. Recurring nudges use hand-set rules; scoped few-shot Allow examples may veto them. Retrieval is different from fine-tuning.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn which model is explained → six nonnegative input rods, eight hidden units and signed bias dial → contributions assemble the output logit; suppress one unit and recompute → network cutaway with exact contributions, not semantic neuron names → trained network at 15%, contribution sum at 35%, intervention at 65% → **65 parameters · 98.33% synthetic holdout · shadow only**; separate hand-set recurring lane stays visible.

scenes.title: Friendly presence, clear limits
utterances: Mira's optional floating companion is implemented with reviewed Show, drag, Open, Hide and Pause controls. Returning from permission settings does not start it.
It requires user-granted access and visible notifications, and stops when the screen turns off. It is not an uninterrupted, always-listening assistant.
Actual overlay, timer, voice and permissioned monitoring still need device tests. Voice is designed as push-to-talk, then transcript review, local understanding and confirmation.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn consent and presence → original Mira window, Show lever, permission gates, Hide/Pause controls and muted microphone → permission return stops before Show; explicit illustrative Show reveals window; screen-off closes it → portrait/environment composition → gates at 20%, distinct controls at 45%, cleanup at 70% → **Implementation · physical proof pending**, no status implying listening.

scenes.title: Research that can say no
utterances: We completed actual local LoRA training, but its semantic performance regressed, so the adapter was rejected. A separate frozen-representation classifier also remains unpromoted.
One hundred eight laptop intervention trials included sixteen restoration controls with identical full logits. Selected channels did not steer reliably better than random controls.
We retain those negative findings. Capturing activations and explaining a tiny classifier do not establish causal understanding of the entire language model.
scenes.visual_intent: Learn rejected evidence is valuable → LoRA adapter branch, separate classifier head, observed tensor and control/patch lanes → rejected candidates detach; sixteen restored-control pairs match, selected and random steering remain comparable → research-bench composition → candidates at 15%, restoration at 40%, negative result at 70% → **Not deployed · no full-model causal understanding**; no invented activation heatmap.

scenes.title: The next honest demonstration
utterances: The laptop consumer already validates bounded exports and computes shadow scores: fifteen tests and actual Java-to-Python synthetic interoperability pass. Office Kit transfer remains pending.
Our Productivity demonstration still needs real iQOO hardware, verified acceleration, permission-tested workflows and a fresh live recording. The public Finale runs October ninth through eleventh.
This is preparation research. Eligible event code and dashboard requirements must be resolved before submission. Mira's promise is practical: local help, understandable decisions, and your control.
